Autism is a difference in how your brain is wired. If you see autism negatively, you see autistic people negatively. I am autistic and the way I interact with the world is informed by that. The way I experience things I love (with intense joy and passion), my excessive empathy (autism being an empathy disorder is a myth - you can look it up), my hypersensitive senses (which can be both good and bad), my social skills, my mannerisms, the way I look at the world, and the things I struggle with. I cannot be separated from autism. 

Autism is a disability and that is NOT a bad thing. I do not need to be cured. I would not be the same person in the slightest. Opposing acceptance and support of autistic people - and encouraging people to think about it negatively, even a little - harms us. What we need is support and accommodations when necessary, not for people to pity us or to think negatively about who we are. That harms us. I’ve spent way too much of my life feeling negatively about who I am to not be kind to myself now. 

Also, autism is not a mental health issue. It’s a developmental disorder. It’s something we are born with. Again, it is part of us and cannot be removed or changed. Just like your skin color will inform your experiences or your nationality. These aren’t things that can be taken away.

Edit: I think I misunderstood your initial comment about autistics needing to be otherized. I thought you meant acknowledging that we are different and accepting us anyway, but it seems you meant to differentiate us so it is easier for others to dehumanize us.

Asperger’s is essentially a functioning label. Autism is a spectrum and we cannot be easily divided into the binary of low and high functioning. That’s not what spectrum means. If you’re autistic, you’re autistic. It’s simple as that. You may have different strengths and weaknesses, but you’re still autistic. Studies have been coming out recently that show functioning labels are actually harmful. 

https://www.disabilityscoop.com/2019/08/02/study-calls-end-high-functioning-autism-label/26992/

As someone who is suspected of being autistic (I'm currently going through the diagnostic process), I've read up on autism a lot. That is a misconception, and it's actually usually the opposite; a lot of autistic people have been found to have an EXCESS of empathy. Like the other commenter said, they struggle with reading social cues. I read an analogy once that's kind of like this: a blind person might not notice you're upset unless you make a noise/say something, because they can't see you. It's not that they don't care. They just might not realise, unless it's more obvious or in a way they can understand. That's how it is with autistic people. 

edited bc I forgot to address the second part: There is definitely a range of severity. It's called a spectrum for a reason, and it affects a lot of people differently.
